# logfire_organization_member (Resource)

Manages the role of an existing member of an organization, by user ID. By default that is the organization of the provider's credential, which the key must be able to read (`organization:read`). On a self-hosted instance, an instance-admin credential acts in another organization with the `organization` argument or the provider `organization`. The API cannot add a member, so the user must already be a member. Creating the resource adopts the member and sets the role. Destroying it removes the user from the organization. The provider API key requires the `organization:read_member` and `organization:write_member` scopes. It needs a Logfire backend from 2026-06-25 (v2026-06-25.01) or newer, which reads the organization of the key and exchanges it.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# The user must already be a member of the organization. Terraform sets the role.
data "logfire_organization_members" "all" {}

resource "logfire_organization_member" "alice" {
  user_id = one([for m in data.logfire_organization_members.all.members : m.id if lower(m.email) == "alice@example.com"])
  role    = "admin"
}

# On a self-hosted instance, an instance-admin key acts in another organization.
data "logfire_organization_members" "team_a" {
  organization = "team-a"
}

resource "logfire_organization_member" "bob" {
  organization = "team-a"
  user_id      = one([for m in data.logfire_organization_members.team_a.members : m.id if lower(m.email) == "bob@example.com"])
  role         = "guest"
}
```

## Existing members only

The Logfire API cannot add a member, so the resource cannot invite anyone. The
user must already be a member of the organization. A user becomes a member
through SSO sign-in with a group mapping, through SCIM, or through an invitation
link. If the user is not a member, the create fails.

Creating the resource adopts the existing member. If the role differs from the
configured one, the provider changes it.

## User ID

The resource identifies the member by `user_id`, which is how the public member
routes identify them. The `logfire_organization_members` data source lists the
user ID of each member with the email address, so a configuration can look a user
up by email address, as in the example above. The `email` and `name` attributes
are read for information and are not inputs.

## Destroy removes the user

Destroying the resource removes the user from the organization. This holds even
when the user was a member before Terraform managed them. The user keeps their
Logfire account but loses access to the organization.

Deleting the resource block from the configuration has the same effect. So does
changing `user_id` or `organization`, which replaces the resource. The replacement
removes the user from the old organization first and then adopts the new member.
The plan does not check that the new user is a member. The API cannot add a user
back, so check that before you change either argument. The plan fails when the new
`user_id` is not known until apply. It also fails when the resource sets no
`organization` and the replacement would create the member in another organization
than the one that holds it, as with the key of another organization. Set
`organization` on the resource then.

Terraform cannot add the user back after a destroy, because the API has no endpoint
that adds a member. To stop managing a member without removing the user, use a
`removed` block with `destroy = false` (Terraform 1.7 or newer) in place of the
resource block:

```terraform
removed {
  from = logfire_organization_member.alice

  lifecycle {
    destroy = false
  }
}
```

Or run `terraform state rm logfire_organization_member.alice` and delete the
resource block. Both leave the user in the organization with their current role.

Destroy treats only the answer "Organization member not found" as an already
removed member. Any other 404, such as one from a backend without the members
routes, fails the destroy and keeps the resource in state.

Logfire refuses to remove or demote the only admin of an organization. The apply
then fails with a 400 error.

## Do not combine with group mappings

SSO sign-in with a group mapping resets the member's role to the mapped role, and
Terraform then reports drift after every sign-in. Do not manage the same member in
this resource and in `logfire_group_mappings`. If a mapping owns the role, ignore it
in the configuration of the member, which still has to set a `role`:

```terraform
resource "logfire_organization_member" "alice" {
  user_id = "0191a5c0-0000-7000-8000-00000000a11c"
  role    = "member"

  lifecycle {
    ignore_changes = [role]
  }
}
```

## Roles

The API accepts only the built-in roles `admin`, `member`, `guest`, and
`billing`. If someone assigns a custom role in the Logfire UI, the provider reads
back its name. The next plan then shows a change to the configured built-in role,
and applying it replaces the custom role.

A Free organization lets its non-owner members hold only the `guest` or `billing`
role, and the owner of a personal organization must remain an admin. The API
rejects other changes with a 422 error. When the organization's plan has no free
seat for a role, the API refuses the change with a 402 error.

## Organization

The provider manages a member only in an organization that it can confirm. By
default that is the organization of the provider's credential, and the key must
be able to read it with `organization:read`, besides the `organization:read_member`
and `organization:write_member` scopes. A key without `organization:read` fails
before any change, and the error names the scope. Key creation does not select
these scopes by default.

On a self-hosted instance, an instance-admin key acts in another organization.
Set `organization` on the resource, or on the provider for every resource of that
provider. The resource argument wins. The provider exchanges the key for a token
that holds both member scopes, so the key itself needs only `instance:admin`. The
exchanged token acts as a service and not as a user, so Logfire does not refuse a
role change or removal because the target holds more permissions. It still
refuses to remove or demote the only admin.

The provider records the ID of the organization in private state, as it does for
a project. The state shows the organization name, and a refresh follows an
organization that was renamed outside Terraform. If the organization is deleted
outside Terraform, a refresh removes the member from state and destroy succeeds.
A key of another organization, or an instance-admin key that names another
organization, fails instead of acting in the organization that the record names.

A member stays in its organization. If the provider `organization` changes and
the resource sets none, the plan fails and names the organization that holds the
member. Set the provider `organization` back, or set `organization` on the
resource, or remove the member from state and import it again. A destroy that
skips the plan check, such as `terraform destroy -refresh=false` or an apply that
removes the resource block, uses the organization that the private state records.

## Schema

### Required

- `role` (String) The member's role: `admin`, `member`, `guest`, or `billing`. A custom role that someone set in the UI is read back by its name, so the next plan shows a change back to this role.
- `user_id` (String) The ID of the user, as `id` in the `logfire_organization_members` data source. Changing it replaces the resource, which removes the previous user from the organization.

### Optional

- `organization` (String) Organization name. Defaults to the provider `organization`, else the organization of the provider credential. Setting it acts in that organization through the instance-admin token exchange (self-hosted only). Changing it replaces the resource, which removes the user from the old organization.

### Read-Only

- `email` (String) The member's email address, for information.
- `id` (String) The user ID.
- `name` (String) The member's name, for information.

## Import

The import ID is the user ID. The member must belong to the organization that the
provider acts in, which is the credential's organization unless the provider sets
`organization`:

```terraform
import {
  to = logfire_organization_member.alice
  id = "0191a5c0-0000-7000-8000-00000000a11c"
}
```

For a member of another organization, use `<organization>/<user_id>`. A user ID
has no slash, so the split is unambiguous. The import needs an instance-admin key
for another organization, and it fails for a key that cannot confirm its
organization:

```terraform
import {
  to = logfire_organization_member.alice
  id = "team-a/0191a5c0-0000-7000-8000-00000000a11c"
}
```

Or use the command line:

```shell
# The import ID is the user ID.
terraform import 'logfire_organization_member.alice' "0191a5c0-0000-7000-8000-00000000a11c"

# For a member of another organization, prefix the organization name.
terraform import 'logfire_organization_member.alice' "team-a/0191a5c0-0000-7000-8000-00000000a11c"
```
